answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a scarce, slashable stake: each identity locks tokens, and endorsements count only when backed by distinct stake that has remained bonded through a challenge window. If a cluster of new accounts all endorse one another, graph checks can trace the spiral back to shared funding and discount that terrace of identities; proven collusion burns their bonded stake. The kernel is that splitting one agent into many names does not multiply voting weight: an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, then risks losing it.
